newsitem.title: YEMEN: Yemen opposition protests over bombing arrests.
newsitem.headline: Yemen opposition protests over bombing arrests.

text.p: Yemeni opposition supporters on Monday held a protest to demand the release of scores of fellow activists arrested following recent bombings in Aden, opposition sources said.
They said "hundreds" of activists staged a one-hour sit-in in front of the office of the attorney general in the town of Mukalla, capital of the southern province of Hadramaut.

The protest was called by five opposition parties including the Yemen Socoalist Party, the main political group in southern Yemen whose leaders' secessionist bid was defeated in a two-month civil war in 1994.

Opposition sources said strikes were planned for Wednesday and Thursday to press the government to free about 120 activists arrested following last month's bombings in Aden, the impoverished Arab country's main southern port city.
Yemeni officials say about 50 people were arrested in connection with the bombings in Aden and that they would go on trial soon. The officials did not say which groups the detainees belonged to.
